description: Mission Forge is a student team passionate about space, mission design, technology, and creative problem-solving. Our members have skills in software/web development, research, data handling, design, and presentation. We collaborate to explore real-world challenges and create practical solutions while learning from each other. Our team is already formed, and we invite existing members to officially join on the platform.
summary:
Orbital Frontier is an interactive, high-fidelity 3D spacecraft engineering lab and orbital mission simulator developed by team MissionForge. Addressing the challenge of making complex aerospace concepts accessible, our platform bridges the gap between theoretical orbital mechanics and intuitive STEM education through real-time WebGL visualization.

Users can assemble multi-stage launch vehicles (such as the historic Saturn V and modern Atlas V architectures), balance mass-to-thrust budgets, calculate orbital trajectories, and simulate high-stakes flight operations. Additionally, the platform reconstructs three landmark NASA mission profiles—Apollo 11, Mars 2020 Perseverance, and Voyager 1—allowing users to explore real flight architectures and telemetry.

Orbital Frontier is vital because space exploration is entering a new golden age; by transforming abstract rocket science formulas into hands-on, physics-informed digital simulations, we inspire and train the next generation of engineers, scientists, and space explorers.
details:
Orbital Frontier operates in modern web browsers as a real-time 3D simulation suite built on React, Three.js, and React Three Fiber:

  1. Rocket Foundry (Modular Assembly): Users construct rockets stage-by-stage (propulsion modules, interstages, avionics, payload adapters, and fairings). The engine dynamically calculates wet and dry mass, thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR), and delta-v (Δv\Delta vΔv) budgets in real time.
    • Apollo 11: Staging, translunar injection, and lunar descent at Mare Tranquillitatis.
    • Mars Perseverance: Interplanetary transfer and entry, descent, and landing (EDL) into Jezero Crater.
    • Voyager 1: Outer Solar System gravitational slingshots and interstellar heliopause trajectory.
  2. NOVA AI Advisory Interface: An in-simulation co-pilot providing real-time telemetry checks, operational guidance, and system status briefings.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing Aerospace Education: Turns abstract physics (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Keplerian orbital elements, Hohmann transfer orbits) into tangible, visual simulations without requiring expensive software.
  • STEM Engagement: Engages students and space enthusiasts through interactive gamified design and historical accuracy.
  • Preserving NASA Exploration History: Functions as an interactive digital archive of humanity’s greatest missions.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies Used

  • Frontend Framework: React 18, Vite, TypeScript/JavaScript
  • 3D Graphics & Physics Visualization: Three.js, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei
  • Styling & Icons: Tailwind CSS, Lucide React
  • Hosting & Deployment: Vercel, GitHub
  • Mathematical Modeling: Keplerian state-vector orbit calculation algorithms, Tsiolkovsky staging calculations

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

  • Balancing Realism with Accessibility: Traditional aerospace tools are intimidating. We engineered a sleek, cyberpunk/mission-control aesthetic paired with guided assembly modes so beginners can build functional rockets while learning genuine aerospace constraints.
  • Cross-Platform Zero-Install Architecture: Engineered entirely client-side in WebGL, running smoothly across standard consumer browsers without plugins or downloads.
